subject: chemistry
question_text: Write the balanced equation for the reaction of H₃BO₃ on heating.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Physics and Chemistry (2026-27 edition), book p.100, chapter 8 p-BLOCK ELEMENTS : GROUP 13, Very Short Answer Questions question 9(d). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints no per-step allocation on any answer in this chapter. This book prints no exam-appearance years for this chapter, so appearances[] is empty — the chapter has long been examined, we simply have no sourced years for this question. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. TWO PRINTED ERRORS CORRECTED. First, the book prints tetraboric acid once as H₂B₃O₇; the formula is H₂B₄O₇, which the same page writes correctly one line above in 4HBO₂ → H₂B₄O₇ + H₂O. Second, the book gives two different temperatures for the second stage — 410 K in its prose and 470 K in its equation — so this card says 'on further heating' and states as a number only the 370 K the book gives consistently for H₃BO₃ → HBO₂. Every equation was balanced atom by atom while authoring, including the overall change B 2 = 2, H 6 = 6, O 6 = 6.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The stages of heating
lines: Orthoboric acid H₃BO₃ loses water in
At 370 K it gives metaboric acid HBO₂:
On further heating it gives tetraboric
At red heat it gives boric oxide B₂O₃:
steps.why: Heating drives water out of the acid one stage at a time: the three OH groups of orthoboric acid are reduced to one in metaboric acid, four HBO₂ units then join into tetraboric acid, and the last water leaves at red heat to give boric oxide.
common_mistakes: Writing tetraboric acid as H₂B₃O₇. The formula is H₂B₄O₇, with four boron atoms.
Stopping at metaboric acid. Strong heating carries the change on to boric oxide B₂O₃.
steps.memory_tip: Water leaves three times: ortho, then meta, then tetra, then the oxide.
steps.margin_note: Name each product — metaboric acid, tetraboric acid, boric oxide.

steps.label: The overall equation
lines: Taking the stages together, two H₃BO₃
lose three water molecules in all:
B₂O₃ is boric oxide, also called boric
steps.why: The overall change is what one balanced equation has to show: two molecules of orthoboric acid carry two boron and six hydrogen atoms, which end as one B₂O₃ and three H₂O.
common_mistakes: Writing H₃BO₃ → B₂O₃ + H₂O. Two acid molecules are needed to supply the two boron atoms of B₂O₃.
Giving two water molecules instead of three. Six hydrogen atoms make three H₂O.
steps.memory_tip: Two acid molecules give one oxide and three waters.
steps.margin_note: The overall equation on its own answers the question; the stages add the detail.

insider_note: The overall equation is the short answer, and naming metaboric acid and boric oxide along the way shows the stages the heating goes through.
